title: Injuries Fatal To Lifelong Savoy Resident
text:
W. G. HODGES.

Injuries Fatal To Lifelong Savoy Resident

SAVOY.—Wiley Green Hodges, 85, widely known farmer and landowner and life-long resident of this community, died at 4 a. m. today in a Sherman hospital as the result of injuries he suffered Sunday afternoon when he fell from a horse near his home here. He sustained a broken hip and fractured ribs.

He was the father of Mrs. Roy Johnson and W. D. Hodges, both of Sherman.

Mr. Hodges was born April 8, 1860, on his father's farm southeast of Savoy. He was married in 1884 to Lenora Herndon, who died in 1932.

In addition to the daughter and son of Sherman, other survivors include four other daughters, Mrs. O. N. Saye of Longview, Mrs. Retta Kincaid of Whitewright, Mrs. T. J. Hollis of Waxahachie and Mrs. Ellis Morgan of Savoy; and two other sons, DeWitt Hodges of Artesia, N. M., and Grover Hodges of Savoy.

Funeral arrangements are incomplete, but services will be held in the Savoy Baptist Church and burial in Sunnyside Cemetery, directed by Earnheart-Strickland Funeral Home.
